::: {.column-page-inset-left}
I am a final year PhD student studying Artificial Intelligence at Stanford.

My advisor is [Scott Linderman](https://lindermanlab.github.io/).

My thesis research focuses on developing and studying methods to parallelize *any* sequential process---well, that is, any discrete-time Markov or stateful process. 

Examples include processes previously believed to be inherently sequential, like the evaluation of nonlinear recurrent neural networks (RNNs).

This ability to parallelize over the sequence length may seem like time travel or magic, but it is just an elegant application of Newton's method! I have proved under what conditions such parallelization techniques can yield dramatic speed-ups over sequential evaluation, and developed scalable and stable parallelization techniques. I call these parallelization techniques the *ungulates*---large hooved mammmals like DEER and ELK.

Artificial intellingence---and numerical computing broadly---are filled with sequential processes that are ripe for parallelizaton! So, please do reach out if you want to develop an ungulate method for your domain of interest!

------

Going forward, I am extremely interested in the quest to develop artificial general intelligence (AGI), and more broadly the study of intelligence---both natural and artificial.

I am particularly interested by:
* developing recurrent (transformer alternative) architectures that can more natively reason
* developing hardware-aware AI algorithms, and novel hardware that can unlock novel AI algorithms
* applying AI to education technology

I'm actively looking for research jobs, so please reach out if you know of a good fit!
